nodes.label: Product Definition v3
nodes.rationale: Current and authoritative. Version 3 narrows the product after direct client confirmation: exactly two user-facing applications and only named administrators signing in to the hotel panel.

nodes.label: Steigenberger Doha Privilege Guest Program
nodes.rationale: An existing invitation-only programme extended personally by the Cluster General Manager, with a printed letter, a numbered card (the reference example is PG-0003) and a printed benefits sheet. What does not exist is any digital surface: members cannot look up benefits on a phone and the hotel has no record of who used what.

nodes.label: Fixed Benefit Discount Schedule
nodes.rationale: F&B 25% (max 6), Rooms 30%, Spa 40% plus 25% retail (max 2), Events 25% (min 20), Lifestyle 30%. Benefits are described as subject to change without notice, which is what makes editability without a code change the single most important configuration requirement.

nodes.label: Member Guest App
nodes.rationale: Four sections: Explore, Offers, Search, Profile. Nothing is hidden behind another tap because the printed sheet it replaces showed everything at once. Redemption history matters more than it appears — it answers 'did I already use the spa discount this month' without a phone call.

nodes.label: Administrator Panel
nodes.rationale: Members, redemptions with export, reporting, and benefit management. The programme currently produces no data at all, so even simple counts are a significant improvement. Test of success: changing the F&B discount from 25% to 20% is a form field, not a code change.

nodes.label: Invitation-Only Onboarding and Claim Flow
nodes.rationale: Runs in the opposite direction from a normal app: administrator creates the record and issues the card, a single-use claim code goes on the invitation letter, the member enters it with their phone, the phone is verified by passcode, consent is captured per channel, and the membership is claimed. A reusable code would let anyone holding a discarded letter join.

nodes.label: Confidentiality of the Membership List
nodes.rationale: The reference card is issued to a member of the Qatari ruling family. A membership list of this kind is a record of named, prominent individuals and their movements — when they dined, when they visited the spa, how often they stay. That is not ordinary customer data, and a leak would be serious independent of any regulatory penalty. Every access-control decision in the build follows from this.

nodes.label: Administrator as the Only Hotel-Facing Account Type
nodes.rationale: No manager, support or outlet-staff logins and no reduced staff panel. Historical database role values may remain solely to preserve attribution on old records; they grant no access and are not shown in the product.

nodes.label: No Points, Tiers or Balances
nodes.rationale: Version 1 assumed a multi-brand coalition with a points currency. All outlets are the hotel's own so there is no settlement between parties; benefits are a fixed discount schedule granted on joining and nothing is earned. If you find yourself writing a balance column, you have misread the specification.

nodes.label: Three-Phase Delivery
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 core (member app, digital card, claim flow, administrator panel, redemption capture, basic reporting, benefit editing). Phase 2 refinement (tap-to-call, push, fuller reporting, optional wallet pass). Phase 3 if wanted (in-app reservations, event RSVPs, PMS integration).

nodes.label: Product Open Questions
nodes.rationale: Question 1 is recorded as resolved. Still open: priority reservations and event invitations, whether staff record bill amounts, member count and growth, expiry or renewal, who issues invitations, the relationship to H Rewards, platform order, Arabic and English, and the three numbers checked every month.
